we propose a hierarchical Keyframe-inpainter model that first generates informative keyframes and their placement and then inpains the sequences between them.

the following question. \emph{What are the most salient and informative events in a temporal sequence?} We propose a model that answers this question by learning to discover keyframes and then inpainting sequences between them.

the problem of discovering keyframes and using these to compactly represent temporal sequences.

we propose a new model for learning keyframe-based representations of temporal sequences and demonstrate that it is effective in discovering informative keyframes and in representing temporal dynamics.

KeyIn learns to discover keyframes and their placement in a sequence and to represent the entire sequence as a sequence of keyframes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
keyframes provide a compact and interpretable way of representing the important information in a sequence, and can be used for downstream tasks such as planning.
a simple keyframe-based hierarchical representation can be learned efficiently by a single end-to-end model, and can be used as a basis for a variety of applications.
a simple hierarchical model with keyframes can learn to reason about complex temporal dynamics in a flexible and compact way.
